team.summary: Founding team consists of the original creators of Apple Siri, with deep technical expertise in AI and prior startup exit experience (Siri acquired by Apple). All three co-founders have strong domain operating experience.

founders.name: Dag Kittlaus
founders.background: Co-founder and CEO; previously a creator of Apple Siri. Prior startup experience with multiple companies.

founders.name: Adam Cheyer
founders.background: Co-founder and VP Engineering; previously a creator of Apple Siri. Strong technical depth in AI and engineering.

founders.name: Chris Brigham
founders.background: Co-founder and Chief Architect; previously worked on Siri. Technical cofounder with architecture/engineering background.

team.technicalDepth: High – all founders have hands-on experience building a major AI assistant (Siri) and the core technology for Viv.

product.plainLanguage: An AI assistant that can perform tasks across multiple apps and services through a conversational interface.

market.sizeHint: [inferred] Large market – virtual assistants for consumers and enterprises; Samsung acquisition indicates significant market potential.
market.competitiveLandscape: [inferred] Competitors included Siri, Google Now, Amazon Alexa, and Microsoft Cortana. Viv's wedge was an open platform allowing third-party integration.
market.whyNow: [inferred] Advances in natural language processing and the proliferation of APIs made a universal assistant feasible; timing aligned with smartphone ecosystem growth.

risks.text: Company was acquired by Samsung in 2016 and is no longer an independent startup; not investable under current thesis.
[inferred] Product may have required significant integration effort for developers, not fully self-serve for SMBs.

subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Founders are the original creators of Siri, with proven founder-market fit, deep technical depth, and prior startup exit (Siri acquired by Apple).

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: Proprietary AI platform with workflow lock-in across apps; not a thin LLM wrapper. However, dependence on platform ecosystems (iOS/Android) and eventual acquisition by Samsung reduce standalone defensibility.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: AI-native agent that takes actions end-to-end, but unclear if self-serve onboarding for SMBs existed; likely required developer integration. One-sentence articulation is possible but not crisp.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: Specific vertical (virtual assistants) with large addressable market; why-now driven by AI advances and API availability. Identifiable competitors and a clear wedge (open platform).

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: Strong signal via acquisition by Samsung, but signal is stale (2016). No recent active usage or funding data available.

scoreRationale: Viv Labs has an exceptional founding team and strong defensibility, but the product may not fully meet the self-serve SMB criteria and traction is outdated. The company is no longer an independent startup, making it unsuitable for current investment under this thesis.
